My dear [Sir William](/person/669)
Would you be so kind as to look at page 9 of the 'Gleanings' at the beginning of the [Musings on the Christian Year](/book/88), and tell me whether you have any recollection of telling [Mr. Keble](/person/798) anything about your opinion of [King Charles](/person/1768)'s truth?[^1]
There is a new edition called for, and [Miss Dyson](/person/464) wants me to take it out. Her letter coming while I was at Salisbury, I asked whether it was there thought that I ought, as it was not according to my impression lightly thrown out, and I put it in because I thought it disproved blind admiration, while showing the real tenderness.
[The Bishop](/person/1015) advised me to ask whether you remembered having said anything of the kind to him - if you did, to leave it; if not, to take it out. So I am acting by order in troubling you about it.
Your affectionate
C. M. Yonge


[^1]: The cult of Charles I was very significant to the Tractarians. In the case of the Hursley group their intense historical consciousness was stimulated by the fact that Richard Cromwell had inhabited the village.
